cards.text: This is Ezekiel talking, a priest living among the exiles (Ezekiel 1:1-3). The word of the LORD comes to him again, with a message for Ezekiel's own people. And it starts with a what-if.
God says: suppose I bring the sword against a land. The people of that land pick one man from among them for a VERY important job.

cards.question: The sword is coming against the land. The people choose a man from among them and appoint him as their ___.

cards.text: Sure enough, the watchman sees it: the sword, coming against the land. Showtime.

cards.question: The watchman sees the sword coming against the land. How does he warn the people?

answers.text: He runs from house to house

cards.text: Somebody hears that horn loud and clear and does NOTHING about it, like a guy who sees his low-fuel light come on and says, "Nah, I can make it." Then the sword comes and takes him away.

cards.question: The man heard the watchman's horn and ignored the warning. When the sword takes him, God says his blood will be on whose head?
God says that if the man who heard the horn had heeded the warning, he would have saved his ___.

cards.text: Now flip it. The watchman SEES the sword coming and never blows the horn, like a smoke detector that smells the smoke and decides it's none of its business.

cards.question: The watchman saw the sword and stayed silent, and the sword takes someone away. God will hold the ___ accountable for that person's blood.

cards.text: Then God drops the what-if and points straight at Ezekiel. Surprise, friend: God has given Ezekiel the watchman's job.

cards.question: God has made Ezekiel a watchman. A watchman for whom?
True or false: The warning Ezekiel gives the people comes from God Himself.

cards.text: Now God makes it personal. Say God tells a wicked man, 'O wicked man, you will surely die,' and Ezekiel doesn't speak out to turn him from his way.

cards.question: God tells a wicked man he will surely die, but Ezekiel doesn't speak out to warn him, and the wicked man dies in his iniquity. What does God say about Ezekiel?

answers.text: God will hold him accountable for the man's blood
God will choose a new watchman in his place
God will overlook it this one time

cards.text: Other side: Ezekiel warns the wicked man to turn from his way, and the man does NOT turn. That's the GPS saying "Make a U-turn" for twenty straight miles while the guy just turns the volume down.

cards.question: True or false: If Ezekiel warns the wicked man and the man refuses to turn, God still holds Ezekiel accountable for his blood.

cards.text: That man still dies in his iniquity, but God tells Ezekiel, 'you will have saved your life.' Ezekiel's job is to blow the horn.
Then God tells Ezekiel to say back to the house of Israel what they've been saying. And friend, it's heavy.

cards.question: What do the people of Israel say is heavy upon them?

answers.text: The long years far from home

cards.text: They say they're wasting away because of them, and they ask, 'How can we live?' Friend, that's less a question and more a sigh with a question mark on the end.
God answers with an oath: 'As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD.' When God swears by His own life, you put the phone DOWN and listen.

cards.question: God answers the people asking how they can live. What does God say He takes no pleasure in?
God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked. What He wants is for the wicked to ___ from their ways and ___.

cards.text: Then God says it straight out: 'Turn! Turn from your evil ways! For why should you die, O house of Israel?' Friend, that is NOT somebody hoping you trip.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel what happens on the day a righteous man sins. True or false: His past righteousness will deliver him on that day.
And on the day a wicked man turns from his wickedness, what does his old wickedness do to him?

cards.text: Picture a righteous man God says will surely live. Then he trusts in his own righteousness and does wrong anyway, like a guy with ten years of perfect parking who decides the fire lane is his now.

cards.question: The righteous man trusted in his righteousness and committed iniquity. Now ___ of his righteous works will be remembered.

cards.text: Now the other guy. God tells a wicked man, 'You will surely die,' and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right.

cards.question: God tells a wicked man, 'You will surely die,' and the man turns from his sin. What does turning look like? Which of these does God say he does?

answers.text: He pays back what he stole

cards.question: True or false: The wicked man who turns will live, but his old sins will still be held against him.

cards.text: None of his sins will be held against him, NONE, and he will surely live. That's opening the bill you've been dreading for months and seeing a balance of ZERO, the kind of bill I'd frame.

cards.question: After all that, what do Ezekiel's people say about the way of the Lord?
True or false: God agrees with the people that His way is not just.

cards.text: God turns it right back around on them: 'But it is their way that is not just.'
So God lays it out one more time, both directions. A righteous man who turns to iniquity will die for it, and a wicked man who turns to what's just and right will live.

cards.question: And STILL the people say the way of the Lord is not just. God answers that He will judge each of them according to his own ___.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen word "watchman," but the setup says only that the people choose a man for an important job. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out "watchman" rather than "judge" or "captain," so this is a guess at the passage's wording rather than a meaning-based blank.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The baker has no basis for reasoning out how many righteous works will be remembered. The earlier teaching that righteousness will not deliver the man does not establish whether none or some works are remembered, making "none" a guess at the unseen wording of verse 13.
